bundles.name: Unit of Account
bundles.description: The monetary unit itself: how it is identified, what kind of unit it is, how it subdivides, and how it is named and presented. This bundle is the referenceable anchor that every sibling model points at when it says 'denominated in'.
bundles.rationale: ISO 4217 governs the identification and minor-unit structure of currencies, funds and precious metals, and ISO 24165 governs digital token units. Both are external registries with their own maintenance cycles, so the unit must be a first-class referenced entity rather than an inline string on payments or balances.

layers.name: Unit Identity and Codes
layers.description: Identifying a monetary unit unambiguously and classifying what kind of unit it is, including units that are not currencies at all.

findings.name: Monetary unit identity and identifier priority
findings.description: A monetary unit is identified by the authoritative registry identifier of its governing scheme before any locally assigned surrogate. For currencies, funds and precious metals this is the ISO 4217 alphabetic code with its numeric code, published by the Maintenance Agency Secretariat; for digital token units it is the nine-character Digital Token Identifier assigned by the DTI Foundation. Alphabetic codes are reused across time after a unit is withdrawn, so a code alone is not a durable key without a scheme and validity interval.

findings.name: Monetary unit kind and monetary character
findings.description: Units carried by the same code scheme are not homogeneous. ISO 4217 covers national and supranational currencies, fund codes and precious-metal units, plus a code reserved for transactions where no currency is involved and a code reserved for testing. Statistical classification separates monetary gold and special drawing rights from currency and deposits. Under MiCA, digital units divide into electronic money tokens referencing a single official currency and asset-referenced tokens referencing other values. An agent must know which of these it holds before treating a value as money.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Unit kind is a set of coded attributes evaluated inline on the unit reference record rather than a separately produced artefact; the underlying taxonomies are externally governed by ISO 4217, MiCA and statistical manuals and are referenced by scheme and version rather than reproduced as a local artefact.

findings.name: SDR as unit of account and reserve asset
findings.description: The SDR is not a currency and not a claim on the IMF. It is an international reserve asset whose value is based on a basket of five currencies (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP) and it is the unit of account of the IMF and some other international organizations. Only IMF members, the IMF and prescribed official holders may hold SDRs; private persons cannot. 2008 SNA classifies SDRs as AF12. ISO 4217 lists XDR as a code for the SDR. Basket weights and daily valuation are properties of the unit, not market FX quotes owned by this model as a price series.

layers.name: Denomination Structure and Presentation
layers.description: How a unit subdivides into minor units and how it is officially named, symbolised and rendered for humans without those renderings becoming semantics.

findings.name: Minor unit exponent and subdivision structure
findings.description: The governing scheme publishes a minor unit value that fixes the number of decimal places in which amounts of the unit are normally expressed. The value is not universally two: some units have zero decimal places, some have three, and some entries have no applicable minor unit at all, notably precious metals and fund codes. Minor unit is a property of the unit, not of a payment or an account, and it constrains the scale of every amount denominated in that unit.

findings.name: Official naming, symbol and presentation
findings.description: A unit carries an official name in the language of its issuing authority, one or more local or transliterated names, and often a symbol. Presentation - symbol placement, digit grouping, negative-amount styling and the choice between symbol and code - is locale-dependent and must not be confused with the unit's semantics. Storing a rendered string in place of a code destroys the ability to reason about the unit.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Names and symbols are inline attributes of the unit reference record; locale rendering rules are governed by external locale repositories and are referenced rather than reproduced, so no separately governed artefact is produced by this model.

bundles.name: Monetary Instrument
bundles.description: The concrete form money takes, treated as a class rather than a holding: its taxonomy, transferability, issuer, the claim and backing behind it, and its character as a settlement asset capable of discharging an obligation.
bundles.rationale: Statistical classification distinguishes currency from transferable and other deposits; accounting standards treat cash and contractual claims as financial assets with a counterparty; PFMI distinguishes central bank money from commercial bank money as settlement assets; and stablecoin guidance recognises assets that are neither. These are attributes of the instrument, independent of who holds it and independent of any particular transfer.

layers.name: Instrument Form and Transferability
layers.description: What kind of instrument this is and how value in it can move, including the medium or ledger the instrument depends on.

findings.name: Instrument form taxonomy
findings.description: Monetary instruments divide by form: physical currency in notes and coin of fixed nominal value that are liabilities of the issuer; transferable deposits exchangeable on demand at par and directly usable for payment; other deposits that are not directly transferable; electronic money as stored monetary value representing a claim on the issuer and issued on receipt of funds; central bank digital currency as a distinct central bank liability intended to coexist with cash; and tokenised units such as electronic money tokens and asset-referenced tokens. Each form carries different claim, transfer and risk properties.

findings.name: Transferability, fungibility and divisibility
findings.description: Whether and how value in the instrument can pass from one party to another: bearer versus registered form, negotiability, fungibility between units of the same class, divisibility down to the minor unit or below, offline transferability, and whether transfer requires the issuer's or an operator's participation. These properties determine what a transfer of the instrument can even mean before any rail is chosen.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Transferability is a set of coded properties on the instrument class specification artefact defined in the sibling finding; producing a second artefact would fragment one governed description of the same class.

findings.name: Retail and wholesale CBDC classes
findings.description: BIS FSI defines CBDCs as a direct liability of the central bank. Retail CBDC is intended for the general public; wholesale CBDC is for financial intermediaries and is like reserves with tokenisation features. Tokenisation is digital representation of a claim on a programmable platform. Architectures include one-tier, pure two-tier/intermediated and hybrid models. BIS legal analysis warns that rCBDC is not a perfect replica of cash because it is intangible, needs a technical system, and may have holding limits, programmability, interest or a contractual user relationship, so classifying it as cash, deposit or e-money imports the wrong legal regime unless lawmakers choose that result. Designation as currency and legal tender may strengthen its monetary-anchor function but is a legal choice. Payment execution on a CBDC platform remains WM-ECO-009; wallets remain WM-ECO-015.

layers.name: Issuer, Claim and Redeemability
layers.description: Who stands behind the instrument, what the holder's claim actually is, what backs it, and on what terms it can be turned back into something else.

findings.name: Issuer identity and issuance authority
findings.description: Every monetary instrument other than a purely decentralised token has an issuer that is a legal entity and that carries the resulting liability. The issuer is referenced by a governed global entity identifier, not by name. The authority to issue derives from a legal basis - treaty or statute for a central bank, an authorisation regime for an electronic money institution, or a crypto-asset authorisation for a token issuer - and that basis is itself evidence that must be recorded and can lapse.

findings.name: Claim, backing and redemption rights
findings.description: What the holder actually owns differs sharply by form. Physical currency is a liability of the issuer at fixed nominal value. Electronic money is stored monetary value representing a claim on the issuer, issued on receipt of funds and redeemable on request. A stablecoin arrangement is expected to give a robust legal claim against the issuer or the reserve assets, redemption at par for single-currency arrangements, reserve assets that are unencumbered and readily convertible, and an effective stabilisation mechanism. Absence of a claim is itself a material, recordable fact.

layers.name: Settlement-Asset Character
layers.description: The instrument viewed as the asset used to discharge obligations: which class of settlement asset it is, and what it contributes to finality.

findings.name: Settlement asset classification and risk profile
findings.description: PFMI Principle 9 requires money settlements in central bank money where practical and available, and requires strict control of credit and liquidity risk where commercial bank money is used instead. Stablecoin guidance recognises a third case: settlement assets that are neither central bank nor commercial bank money and that carry additional financial risk. Classifying the instrument into one of these classes, with its credit and liquidity risk attributes, is a property of the instrument and is needed before any rail selection.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Settlement asset classification is a coded assessment recorded on the instrument class specification and justified by the issuer authority dossier; the underlying PFMI assessments are produced and published by supervisory authorities under their own governance, so this model references them rather than generating an artefact.

findings.name: Discharge and finality properties of the instrument
findings.description: Two distinct properties are often conflated. Legal tender status confers, in principle, mandatory acceptance at full face value with power to discharge a payment obligation, subject to good-faith refusal, contractual agreement on other means, and anti-money-laundering limits. Settlement finality is the irrevocability and unconditionality of a transfer under an arrangement's rules and legal basis. This model records the instrument-side contribution: what the delivery of the instrument itself accomplishes in law. The transfer arrangement that confers finality is owned by the payment model.

bundles.name: Legal Status and Jurisdiction
bundles.description: Where and on what terms the unit or instrument is lawful money, who is authorised to issue it, and what restrictions bound its holding and use.
bundles.rationale: Legal tender is conferred by specific legal instruments and is bounded rather than absolute; issuance is subject to authorisation regimes that can be granted, varied and withdrawn; and holding or usage limits are real constraints that change how an agent may reason about the instrument. None of this is derivable from the code list alone.

layers.name: Legal Tender and Territorial Validity
layers.description: The jurisdictional footprint of the unit and instrument, and the acceptance obligations that attach within it.

findings.name: Legal tender status and its limits
findings.description: Legal tender status is conferred by specific legal instruments and its effects are not defined uniformly. In the euro area, treaty provisions confer status on banknotes and a Council regulation on coins, while the concept itself is defined through recommendation and case law as mandatory acceptance at full face value with power to discharge. The same regulation caps obligatory acceptance at fifty coins in a single payment, proving that legal tender is quantitatively bounded. Status must therefore be asserted per jurisdiction, per instrument form, with its limits.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Legal tender assertions are recorded on the discharge status assertion artefact defined under the settlement-asset layer; duplicating them as a second artefact would create two governed statements of the same legal fact and invite divergence.

findings.name: Territorial validity and monetary sovereignty
findings.description: A unit's jurisdictional footprint is not the same as its issuer's jurisdiction. A currency may be substituted for national units across a monetary union, adopted unilaterally by a jurisdiction that does not issue it, circulate alongside a domestic unit, or be lawful in dependent territories on different terms. This finding records the set of jurisdictions in which the unit functions as money and the basis on which it does so.

layers.name: Authorisation and Usage Restrictions
layers.description: The supervisory permission behind the instrument and the restrictions that bound how it may be held, converted or used.

findings.name: Issuer authorisation and supervisory status
findings.description: Issuing electronic money or a token that references an official currency is a regulated activity in many jurisdictions, subject to authorisation, prudential requirements including own funds and safeguarding of received funds, and ongoing supervision. Authorisation is granted by a named competent authority, has a register entry, can be passported across a union, and can be varied, suspended or withdrawn. The current status is a time-bounded fact requiring its own observation timestamp.

findings.name: Holding, conversion and usage restrictions
findings.description: Restrictions bound how much of an instrument may be held, whether it may be converted, and who may use it. Sources include design decisions such as holding limits contemplated for retail central bank digital currency, convertibility controls imposed by monetary authorities, prohibitions on interest-bearing use, and restrictive measures against specified parties. These are properties of the unit or instrument in a jurisdiction, not of any one account, and they must be time-bounded and jurisdiction-scoped.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Restrictions are referenced by pointer to externally maintained authoritative lists that are versioned and republished by their owning authorities; copying them into a local artefact would create a stale shadow of a fast-moving legal source and is deliberately avoided.

bundles.name: Lifecycle and Succession
bundles.description: How units and instrument series come into being, change identity, and cease - including the continuity rules that let historical records remain interpretable.
bundles.rationale: Amendment 180 moving Bulgaria from BGN to EUR, the withdrawal of the EUR 500 note from issuance, and the maintenance of a separate historic code list all demonstrate that units and instrument series have distinct, dated lifecycles whose transitions must be modelled explicitly rather than inferred from a current-state snapshot.

layers.name: Unit Lifecycle and Succession
layers.description: States of a monetary unit over time and the mappings that link a retired unit to what replaced it.

findings.name: Unit lifecycle states and effective dating
findings.description: The governing registry maintains current codes separately from historic denominations, and each change is issued as a numbered amendment with an effective date. A unit therefore moves through states - announced, current, superseded, historic - and the model must record both the date the change takes legal or registry effect and the date the local record observed it, because these differ and downstream restatements depend on the distinction.

findings.name: Succession, redenomination and continuity of contracts
findings.description: When a unit is replaced, historical amounts must remain interpretable. Euro introduction supplies the normative pattern: continuity of legal instruments is preserved, conversion rates are fixed and irrevocable, expressed as one unit of the new currency in terms of the old with six significant figures, and inverse or derived rates must not be substituted. Redenomination without substitution - dropping zeros in a currency reform - raises the same restatement problem with a different mechanism.

layers.name: Instrument Series and Stock Lifecycle
layers.description: Series and issue lifecycle of an instrument class, and the rules for withdrawal, demonetisation and exchange - at class level, never at holding level.

findings.name: Instrument series, denominations and issue
findings.description: An instrument class is issued in series with defined denomination sets. Euro banknotes illustrate this: a first series of seven denominations and a second series in which one denomination was not continued. For token instruments the analogue is the deployed contract version and the ledger on which it is deployed, together with fork history. Series identity matters because acceptance, exchange and validation rules can differ by series.

findings.name: Withdrawal, demonetisation and exchange guarantees
findings.description: Ceasing to issue an instrument is distinct from removing its legal tender status, and both are distinct from ending the ability to exchange it. A denomination may stop being issued while remaining legal tender and exchangeable indefinitely at the issuing central banks. For electronic money and tokens, the corresponding event is termination of the issuance programme with a redemption obligation that survives it. Conflating these three transitions produces incorrect conclusions about whether value can still be realised.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Withdrawal and exchange facts are recorded as dated transitions on the instrument series catalogue artefact; issuing a separate artefact would split a single series timeline across two governed records and make the ordering of transitions ambiguous.

bundles.name: Amount and Conversion
bundles.description: The monetary amount as a value object composed by every sibling model, and the arithmetic and rate-provenance rules that make amounts comparable and convertible without silent corruption.
bundles.rationale: Amounts are always a pair of a numeric value and a unit reference, are constrained in scale by the unit's minor unit and again by the target payload's data type, and conversion is governed by explicit legal rules in at least one major case: fixed rates at six significant figures, no rounding of the rate, no derived inverse rates and round-half-up on the result.

layers.name: Monetary Amount Value Object
layers.description: The structure, precision and arithmetic of a monetary amount, independent of what is being paid for.

findings.name: Amount structure, scale and sign
findings.description: A monetary amount is inseparably a numeric value plus a reference to the unit that denominates it; a bare number is not an amount. Financial messaging types bind the two together and impose their own total and fractional digit limits, which may be narrower than the unit's minor unit. Sign conventions, zero and the prohibition on binary floating point for exact decimal values are part of the value object's contract, not of any consuming model.

findings.name: Rounding, arithmetic and allocation rules
findings.description: Conversion arithmetic is legally constrained in at least one authoritative case: the conversion rate must not itself be rounded or truncated, inverse rates derived from it must not be used, and a converted result landing exactly halfway is rounded up. Beyond conversion, allocation of a total across parts must not create or destroy value, which requires an explicit remainder rule. These rules belong to the amount, not to any consuming process, so that all consumers round identically.

layers.name: Conversion and Rate Reference
layers.description: The definitional side of converting between units: the ordered pair, the rate type, and the provenance and fitness for use of any rate relied upon.

findings.name: Currency pair, rate type and rate provenance
findings.description: A rate is meaningless without an ordered pair, a quotation convention, a rate type and a provenance record. Rate types differ fundamentally: a legally fixed conversion factor is irrevocable and directional, while a published reference rate is an observation computed at a stated time under a stated procedure and may carry an explicit caveat against use for transactions. Publication can also be suspended for a pair when representative rates cannot be established, so a rate reference must record availability as well as value.

bundles.name: Governance, Alignment and Assurance
bundles.description: How the local record stays faithful to its authoritative sources, how it maps to external schemes without over-claiming conformance, and how it is validated, published, retained and accessed.
bundles.rationale: Every substantive fact in this model is sourced from an externally governed registry, legal instrument or standard that versions independently. The model must therefore carry explicit provenance, alignment-not-conformance semantics, validation evidence and retention rules, or agents will silently consume stale or mis-mapped monetary reference data.

layers.name: Authority, Provenance and Stewardship
layers.description: Which body governs each fact, how changes are tracked, and who is accountable for the local record.

findings.name: Authoritative source, amendment tracking and record stewardship
findings.description: Different facts in this model have different masters: the currency code and minor unit are governed by the ISO 4217 maintenance agency secretariat, digital token identifiers by the DTI registration authority, entity identifiers by the LEI issuer network, legal tender by legislators, and authorisation by competent authorities. The local record is a derived copy that must name its master per field, track that master's amendment stream, and name a steward accountable for the copy. The registry names the holder and settlement rail operator as maintainers; for the unit and instrument definitions themselves the accountable steward is the issuing or maintaining authority's designated counterpart in the adopting Dimension.

layers.name: External Alignment and Payload Interoperability
layers.description: Mapping to external code schemes and message formats as alignments, with conflicts recorded rather than smoothed over.

findings.name: Code-scheme alignment and recorded conflicts
findings.description: The same economic thing can be identified in several schemes at once - a token pegged to an official currency may carry a digital token identifier while also referencing an ISO 4217 code, and national schemes may use codes that clash with the international list. Alignment is a mapping with a stated equivalence strength, not a claim of conformance. Where schemes disagree - for example on whether a unit is money at all, or on effective dates for a substitution - the conflict is recorded and neither side is silently preferred.

findings.name: Payload and projection interoperability
findings.description: Messaging standards bind amount and currency together in dedicated data types and externalise volatile code sets that are republished on their own cadence. Projecting this model into a payload therefore constrains scale, code-set membership and the permitted set of codes, and a projection that silently truncates or substitutes is a defect. Storage and interface choices - documents, message schemas, tool interfaces or database collections - are projections that must round-trip the semantics defined here.

layers.name: Validation, Access and Retention
layers.description: Proving the record is correct, controlling who may see which parts of it, and governing how long superseded states are kept.

findings.name: Validation rules and supporting evidence
findings.description: Monetary reference data admits strong mechanical checks: code format and check-character validation for identifiers that define one, cross-checking alphabetic against numeric codes, verifying minor unit against the authoritative list, confirming that an amount's scale satisfies both unit and payload constraints, and confirming that an entity identifier resolves in its register with an active status. Each check produces evidence with its own observation timestamp, distinct from the effective time of the fact checked.

findings.name: Access, retention and publication of monetary reference data
findings.description: Most of this model is public reference data that authoritative bodies publish free of charge and permit free reuse, which argues for open read access. But not all of it is: authorisation checks, restrictive-measure linkages, reserve attestations and supplier-licensed rate feeds carry licence, confidentiality or redistribution constraints. Retention is asymmetric to deletion: superseded unit states and succession mappings must be kept indefinitely to keep historical amounts interpretable, while cached third-party feeds may be subject to contractual deletion.

model.name: Price / Valuation
model.purpose: Represent observed prices, subject-specific valuation conclusions and statistical price or index observations as governed, versioned value assertions independent of storage or exchange format.
model.scope_statement: Owns value-assertion identity and family, subject and interest bindings, amount and unit semantics, price observation evidence, appraisal engagement, basis, approaches, inputs, assumptions, conclusion and uncertainty, price-index structure, provenance, correction and standards projections while referencing offers, transactions, invoices, payments, contracts, assets, currencies, official statistics, datasets and documents.
in_scope: Value assertion identity, subject, interest or basket, quantity, amount, unit, currency, context and effective time
Price observations and components, appraisal engagements, bases, premises, methods, inputs, comparables, adjustments, conclusions, uncertainty and review
Price-index baskets, classifications, weights, formulae, periods, observations, releases, revisions, provenance, conversion, access and interoperability
out_of_scope: Offer, order, contract, trade, transaction, invoice, payment, tax, insurance, asset, liability, product, service, currency or commodity master lifecycles
Respondent-level source data, generic official-statistics production, dataset and file distribution, document payload, publication channel and party identity
Universal asset-class methods, jurisdictional valuation law, accounting recognition, tax rules, disclosure thresholds, foreign-exchange rate authority or price-index formula

boundary_notes.distinction: This model may observe requested, quoted, administered or transacted amounts, but the commercial record owns negotiation, agreement, performance and legal effect.
Invoiced and paid amounts are external accounting or settlement events; they may evidence price but do not become appraisal or index conclusions.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Asset, Liability, Product, Service and Right
boundary_notes.distinction: The valued subject and interest retain external identity, physical or legal properties and lifecycle while this model owns only the scoped value assertion.
Currency codes and rate observations are external masters; a derived conversion retains original amount, rate binding, time, direction and rounding.
This model specializes price-index semantics and calculations while Official Statistics owns programme authority, release governance, statistical quality and general observation-vintage lifecycle.
Datasets, valuation reports, workfiles and snapshots are referenced artifacts; none replaces the logical value assertion, method or immutable revision.

functions.name: Register value assertion
functions.description: Register assertion family, subject, interest, unit, context and immutable identity.
preconditions: subject and authority resolve
effects: assertion becomes governed without claiming universal truth

functions.name: Record price observation
functions.description: Append a sourced listing, quote, administered, negotiated or transaction price observation.
preconditions: capture and unit checks pass
effects: original observed amount and terms remain immutable

functions.name: Correct price observation
functions.description: Create a successor observation with correction reason and evidence.
preconditions: correction authority resolves
effects: prior observation remains available and marked

functions.name: Normalize price components
functions.description: Derive comparable gross, net or unit views without destroying original terms.
preconditions: inclusions, quantity and rounding resolve
effects: derived amount carries transformation lineage

functions.name: Commission appraisal
functions.description: Register purpose, scope, client, intended users, valuer and basis.
preconditions: competence and conflicts are assessed
effects: assignment boundary and permitted reliance become explicit

functions.name: Register valuation inputs
functions.description: Record inspections, sources, assumptions, comparables, models and adjustments.
preconditions: input quality and access permit use
effects: each indication becomes reproducible and attributable

functions.name: Reconcile value conclusion
functions.description: Reconcile approach and scenario indications into a scoped conclusion.
preconditions: material inputs and uncertainty are disclosed
effects: conclusion retains rejected results and rationale

functions.name: Issue, review or withdraw valuation
functions.description: Approve, review, supersede, expire or withdraw a valuation conclusion.
preconditions: authorized sign-off resolves
effects: lifecycle state changes without erasing prior opinions

functions.name: Define price index
functions.description: Register index purpose, coverage, basket, classifications, weights and formulae.
preconditions: statistical authority and structure resolve
effects: index semantics become reproducible

functions.name: Calculate and release index
functions.description: Compile a complete series observation and bind it to an Official Statistics vintage.
preconditions: quality and release checks pass
effects: published value retains contributors, status and lineage

functions.name: Revise index observation
functions.description: Create a successor index vintage for correction, revised inputs, rebasing or methodological change.
preconditions: revision policy permits change
effects: prior release remains resolvable

functions.name: Convert or export value
functions.description: Convert currency or produce a standards-aligned projection with validation and loss declaration.
preconditions: versions, rate and permissions resolve
effects: original value, conversion and information loss remain explicit

composition.target: Offer, Contract, Transaction, Invoice and Payment models
composition.purpose: Binds requested, agreed, invoiced or paid amounts without importing commercial or settlement lifecycle.

composition.target: Asset, Liability, Product, Service and Right models
composition.purpose: Identifies the subject and interest while external masters own their properties and lifecycle.
Resolves maintained currency codes and conversion rates while preserving original value semantics.
Combines price-index specialization with general statistical authority, quality, release and vintage governance.

composition.target: Dataset, Report, Publication and Evidence models
composition.purpose: Connects workfiles, source snapshots, reports and distributions without treating them as the logical value assertion.
Supports pinned valuation-process and reporting profiles without asserting conformance from structure alone.
Supports accounting fair-value measurement profiles only where another applicable standard requires or permits them.
Supports statistical and commerce-facing projections with pinned versions, validation and declared loss.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner, price-observation authority, valuation authority, statistical compiler, semantic steward and disclosure authority.
Declare subject or asset, contract, offer, transaction, invoice, payment, currency, market, statistics, dataset, document and party master systems.
Publish model, object, event, relation, classification, access, retention, assurance and interoperability registries.
Pin valuation basis, asset class, jurisdiction, price-index, currency, confidentiality and exchange profiles.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint value-assertion identifiers only in the adopting Dimension's governed namespace; preserve asset, offer, transaction, invoice, payment, IVS, IFRS, SDMX, GS1 and currency identifiers as typed references with authority, version and time.
registry_links: https://ver.cy/models/
https://ver.cy/model-agent-protocol.md
Dimension-local subject, value assertion, market, currency, statistics, access and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, value-assertion master ID, immutable revision and explicit authority; never use subject name, numeric amount, date, report filename or hash alone as identity.
Keep observed, requested, agreed, invoiced, paid, accounting, appraised, modelled and indexed values distinct and preserve corrected, superseded or withdrawn revisions.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, assertion family, subject profile, basis, source, method, rationale, access and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior assertion revisions.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when assertion identity, subject, interest, quantity, unit, time, basis, method, provenance and access meaning remain intact.
IVS, IFRS, SDMX, GS1 and partner mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative valuation or price master-system identifier and immutable revision identifier.
Governed globally resolvable value-assertion or index-observation IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep effective, observation, inspection, valuation, release, conversion and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {assertion-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a subject name, amount, date, filename or hash alone as assertion identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and method versions, currency or unit, effective time, provenance, assurance and access marking for every retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may observe, appraise, calculate, review, correct, convert, disclose, rely on, supersede, withdraw, retain and tombstone value assertions.
Every value requires assertion family, subject or basket, interest, quantity, currency or unit, context, effective time, source, method, status, uncertainty and revision lineage as applicable.
Agents never infer transaction completion, accounting recognition, market value, fair value, appraisal compliance, cost of living or inflation from a bare amount or index movement.
Offers, transactions, invoices, payments, contracts, subjects, currencies, statistics, datasets and documents remain in their owning systems and are referenced.

Automated agents may append low-risk observations and derived projections under delegation but consequential valuation, reliance, disclosure, withdrawal and irreversible use decisions default to proposal or confirmation.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, assertion family, subject and interest, unit, effective time, requested revision, basis, assurance and access policy; return the minimum permitted projection.
create: Create stable assertion identity, family, subject and interest binding, original amount or range, unit, time, source, method and explicit unknowns before derived normalization or release.
update: Append an immutable revision with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor; validate subject, units, basis, method, evidence, uncertainty and access before and after mutation.
delete: Apply retention, legal hold, reliance and evidence policy; tombstone assertions or withdraw projections while preserving identity, issued revisions and non-cascading external references.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Own namespace, mastership, delegation, access, retention and federation rules.

roles.name: Price observer or source steward
responsibilities: Capture original prices, terms, evidence, sample role and corrections.

roles.name: Valuer or valuation authority
responsibilities: Own appraisal scope, methods, judgement, conclusion and professional accountability.

roles.name: Statistical compiler
responsibilities: Own index scope, basket, weights, formula, observations and release binding.

roles.name: Method and data steward
responsibilities: Govern definitions, units, sources, models, quality and crosswalks.

roles.name: Reviewer or auditor
responsibilities: Review evidence, assumptions, calculations, changes and conflicts without rewriting originals.

roles.name: Disclosure and reliance authority
responsibilities: Approve recipients, intended use, confidentiality, embargo and reliance rights.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive disclosure unless the active Dimension, role, purpose, assertion family, subject and field policy grant the action; expose the minimum necessary projection.
exceptions: Emergency access must be time-limited, purpose-bound, attributable, independently reviewed and unable to erase immutable history, evidence, reliance limits or legal hold.
audit_requirements: Log actor, role, purpose, assertion and revision identity, action, decision, policy and method versions, RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, affected scope and outcome for privileged mutation, conversion, reliance or disclosure.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension-owner AGENTS.md, subject master, active valuation, accounting, statistics, currency, access and retention policies.
Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required offer, transaction, invoice, payment, asset, statistics, dataset and document model instructions before mutation.

coverage.claim: A source-grounded reviewable draft of Price / Valuation across IVS, IFRS 13, Eurostat HICP, the IMF CPI Manual, European Union price-index law, GS1 price vocabulary, SDMX, ISO currency codes, W3C provenance and IETF time standards, without a claim of universal asset-class, jurisdictional or accounting completeness.

checklist.notes: Value assertion, subject, interest, observation, appraisal conclusion, index observation and immutable revision identities are distinct.
Observed, quoted, administered, transaction, accounting, appraisal, model and index families plus bases and price components are explicit.
The informational object's own amount, currency, unit, range, precision, basis, status and effective time are represented; physical subject properties stay external.
Agents distinguish assertion families using source event, terms, authority, method, market context and evidence.
Capture, engagement, calculation, issue, review, correction, revision, supersession, expiry and withdrawal preserve history.
Subjects, rights, markets, parties, sources, offers, transactions, statistics, currencies, datasets and reports use typed bindings.
Effective, observation, inspection, valuation, reference, release, conversion and ingestion times remain distinct.
Sources, evidence snapshots, activities, agents, methods, inputs, models, transformations and revisions are linked.
Dimension owner, observer, valuer, compiler, steward, reviewer and disclosure authority have separate responsibilities.
Subject, unit, component, method, input, formula, uncertainty, sensitivity, index and crosswalk checks are explicit.
Confidentiality, embargo, intended user, permitted reliance, minimum projections and audit are represented.
Immutable revisions, withdrawal, tombstones, reliance evidence, retention and legal hold are explicit.
IVS, IFRS, HICP, CPI, SDMX, GS1 and ISO currency bindings pin versions and disclose loss.
Observation, correction, normalization, appraisal, review, index compilation, conversion and projection functions declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Asset-class, jurisdiction, accounting, tax, insurance and regulatory profiles must provide exact valuation bases, mandatory procedures and reliance consequences.
Offer, transaction, invoice, payment, contract, asset, currency, Official Statistics, dataset and report lifecycles remain in neighboring models.
Certified external field crosswalks, appraisal conformance checklists and domain-specific index calculation suites remain future work.
conflicts: The aggregate combines price observations, professional valuation conclusions and statistical price indices because all are governed value assertions, but their authority, method and lifecycle remain strictly typed.
IFRS 13 fair value is an accounting measurement framework applied when another standard requires or permits it; it is not a universal synonym for market value or transaction price.
A price index does not directly equal an individual item's price, cost of living or universal inflation and requires population, basket, weights, formula and reference-period interpretation.
regional_assumptions: Regulation (EU) 2016/792 and HICP methodology define a European statistical profile, not universal price or index law.
IVS effective 31 January 2025 is treated as the current international valuation reference; the 2028 material is only an exposure draft and is not used normatively.
ISO 4217:2015 codes are mutable through the appointed maintenance agency, so adopting Dimensions must retain the code-list version or retrieval time.
